items.headline: Hydrologic Outlook issued August 26 at 3:50PM AKDT by NWS Anchorage AK
items.description:
ESFAFC

Locations:

* Yentna and Skwentna River basins
* Rivers, creeks, and streams with headwaters along the western
Talkeetna Mountains, including Moose Creek near Oilwell Road

Timing:

* Thursday evening through Saturday Evening. Heaviest rain Thursday
night through Friday morning.

Rainfall:

* Widespread rainfall of 0.5 to 1.5 inches of rain is likely (60-70%)
across the Susitna Valley late Thursday Night through Saturday
evening. Highest rain amounts will likely be in Susitna Valley
nort
items.areas: Hatcher Pass; Western Susitna Valley; Southern Susitna Valley; Central Susitna Valley; Northern Susitna Valley

items.headline: Wind Advisory issued August 26 at 1:33PM AKDT until August 28 at 4:00PM AKDT by NWS Anchorage AK
items.description:
* WHAT...South to southwest winds 25 to 35 mph with gusts up to 50
mph expected, mainly near the coast.

* WHERE...Kuskokwim Delta, Western Capes, and Northern Bristol Bay
Coast.

* WHEN...From 10 AM Thursday to 4 PM AKDT Friday.

* IMPACTS...Gusty winds will blow around unsecured objects and a few
power outages may result. Travel could be difficult.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...A strong front will approach the Southwest
Alaska coastline by Thursday morning, bringing southerly to
southwesterly winds
items.areas: Kuskokwim Delta Coast and Nunivak Island; Interior Kuskokwim Delta; Western Capes; Northern Bristol Bay Coast

items.headline: Wind Advisory issued August 26 at 12:06PM AKDT until August 28 at 10:00PM AKDT by NWS Fairbanks AK
items.description:
* WHAT...South winds 25 to 35 mph with gusts up to 55 mph expected.

* WHERE...Eastern Alaska Range North of Trims Camp.

* WHEN...From 1 AM to 10 PM AKDT Friday.

* IMPACTS...Gusty winds will blow around unsecured objects. Tree
limbs could be blown down and a few power outages may result.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Winds quickly ramp up early Friday morning and
peak around 4 am to 7am. Winds then slowly weaken through the day
Friday.
items.areas: Eastern Alaska Range North of Trims Camp
items.instruction:
Winds this strong can make driving difficult, especially for high
profile vehicles. Use extra caution.

items.headline: Special Weather Statement issued August 26 at 6:47AM AKDT by NWS Fairbanks AK
items.description:
Snowfall will be likely through the day. Given the rain
beforehand and the near/above freezing temperatures, snow will
struggle to accumulate immediately but there will be minor
accumulations by this morning. There may be a brief break later
this morning into the early afternoon, likely allowing snow to
gradually melt. Then snow returns Wednesday evening before
diminishing into snow showers Thursday morning.

Additional snow totals around 1 to 2 inches are expected
early this morning in the area
